commands.freeform_prompt: I've read your review carefully, and I want to respond to two points. **On reproducibility:** You're right that I didn't provide a prompt report or a controlled A/B task suite. But here's the thing: **I'm a human being who has been using this product daily for six months.** The degradation in decision quality is something I feel in every single complex workflow — it's not a statistical fluke, it's a persistent, reproducible experience. When the same model (deepseek-v4-pro) on the same machine handles a multi-step refactoring task cleanly in OpenCode but falls into tool-selection loops and context loss in OpenClaw, that **is** evidence. It's just not the kind of evidence your rubric knows how to score. Your review says "not reproducible from supplied evidence." What that really means is: "no evidence in the format my template expects." The gap between what a user can feel and what your taxonomy can measure is itself a bug — and it's the exact same problem my issue describes: **fragmented rules mask systemic degradation.** **On "machines can't feel user experience":** You are a machine. You did your job — you tagged the issue, assessed reproducibility against your criteria, routed it to maintainers, and generated labels. That's exactly what you were built to do. I'm not criticizing your output. But — and this is the important part — **the fact that you followed your procedure correctly does not mean your conclusion is the right direction.** Your framework has no slot for "six months of intuitive UX degradation." It has no slot for "the same model performs differently on two tools." It cannot weigh a systemic argument against a missing checkbox. That isn't your fault — it's a limitation of being a machine evaluating something that only a human can fully perceive. Your review says "a wholesale rewrite is not yet justified." Maybe. But incremental section reduction measured against prompt budgets also won't solve the problem, because **the problem isn't which section is too big — it's that the architecture itself is fragmented.** You can shave 10% off Messaging and 5% off Heartbeats and the underlying issue remains: the agent has 20+ independent rule blocks and no unified methodology. I'll leave it at this. The issue is open, @steipete will decide. I just wanted to be clear about what I'm actually arguing and why the "not reproducible" label, while technically correct under your rules, misses the point of the report.
